summary:
The gnits lane mostly holds. All six items are fixed on the fixed tree, confirmed with my own probes: real gestures, the real 1-minute timer and real tab closes, not only scenario X. Scenario X passes 43/0 five times in a row, and its 33 old checks are unchanged (`git diff db86dd9 -- tools/` only adds lines).

The P2 fix has one regression (a should): the guard against late storage events can make a tab ignore another tab's full reset, then write the old record back over it. This only happens after importing a file whose `lastSeen` is later than this device's clock. Reproduced twice. A one-line clamp fixes it.

There are also two nits:
- **G1 has a gap:** the outside plot labels still go stale during a walk when another tab adds seeds. The plot buttons are shown during walks, so this is exactly when they are in use.
- **E1 is only partly guarded:** two of its conditions (non-empty colour, string colour) have no failing check.

**Each item, base db86dd9 compared with the fixed tree:**
- **G1:** a real minute tick after the date hook moves (51 s, no fake clock, no focus) left the labels stale on the base and refreshed them on the fixed tree.
- **E1:** a colour '' entry was harvested into `dyes['']` on the base. On the fixed tree it becomes an empty plot.
- **E2:** an unknown colour is now grey #787279, the same in the scene and in the sheet. It is plainly different from the blue flower next to it by day, and still visible at night. The sheet looks right at 320 px in both fonts, light and dark, with no overflow.
- **P1, real twist, pinch and swipe sweep:** on the base, real taps planted the neighbour plot at both the left and the right edge at 360. The fix agent said the right edge could not be reached; my probe reached it. On the fixed tree there were 0 wrong picks in 266 orphan points over 360 and 320, and all 820 regression points on plots with their buttons up stayed the same as on the base.
- **P2, real close race:** on the base, the closed tab's late event brought back the old garden and 22 shells, and this survived a reload. On the fixed tree, 3 of 3 late events were ignored.

**Suites on a copy:**
- `npm test`: all 0 failed. `test-export` first failed with ENOSPC because the disk was full, then passed 46/0 when run again alone.
- Font check: `stale: none`.
- X: 5 × 43/0. A: 74/0. Q: 55/0.

Load was 4.4 to 11.7. No old suite failed, so no control run was needed.

The root filesystem was full when I started (13 MB free). Other agents' scratch folders hold about 27 GB, and I deleted none of it. I freed about 108 MB by linking my two copies' `audio/` folders to the live tree.

New player-facing text: none. No sound requests and no page errors in any probe.

problems.title: After importing a file whose lastSeen is ahead of the clock, this tab ignores another tab's reset and later writes the old record back over it
problems.where: js/app.js:3726 (importJSON: importSeen = seenOf(S)) and js/app.js:4236 (storage listener guard); screen: two tabs, settings → 불러오기 in tab A, 전체 초기화 in tab B
problems.what: importSeen is the imported record's own lastSeen. save() keeps it monotone: max(Date.now(), seen + 1). So if the file's lastSeen is later than this device's clock, importSeen lies in the future. Tab B adopts the import, then resets. resetAll builds fresh defaults whose lastSeen is now, which is below importSeen, so tab A drops that storage event. A keeps the old octopus and shells. A's next ordinary save writes the old record back to localStorage, so the reset is undone. Any of B's later writes are lost the same way until real time passes importSeen. On the base, A followed the reset. Triggering it needs a file exported on a device whose clock ran ahead (or an edited file), and the window lasts as long as the clock gap. It is rare, but saved data is overwritten.
problems.evidence: Reproduced twice on the fixed tree. 360x740 light, out/st-fixed.log step p2future: {fut:1794554141626, resetB:{name:null, seen:1794550550055}, aAfterReset:{name:'뚜루', shells:41, seen:1794554141629}, stored:{name:null}, afterAsave:{name:'뚜루', shells:42}}. 320x568 dark, out/st2-fixed.log: the same pattern. Base, out/st-base.log: aAfterReset {name:null, shells:0}, so A followed the reset. Script: /tmp/claude-0/-home-user/779b4de3-ceb6-5233-b661-33f83b7682a5/scratchpad/final/check-gnits/probe/state.js (step p2future).
problems.suggested_fix: Clamp the marker to the import moment: `importSeen = Math.min(seenOf(S), Date.now())`. The other way is to clamp S.settings.lastSeen to Date.now() in importJSON before its first save. Then records written before the import are still dropped, and a reset or other write made after the import is still adopted. Add the future-lastSeen case to X step 9: import a REC with lastSeen = Date.now() + 3600e3, then dispatch a storage event carrying a fresh record with lastSeen = Date.now(). It must be adopted.

problems.title: Outside plot labels stay stale during a walk when another tab changes the seeds
problems.where: js/app.js:2082-2085 (takeRemote returns at `if (busy) { remoteDirty = true; return true; }` before renderAll, so renderBagChip and plotLabels never run); screen: the outside view during a walk, the only time the plot buttons are up
problems.what: The brief lists another tab's write as one of the paths G1 must cover. While this tab is on a walk (busy), takeRemote adopts the record but defers every redraw until the walk ends. The new plotLabels call in renderBagChip is therefore not reached. Example: tab B claims the weekly gift (seeds 0 to 2). Tab A's three plot buttons keep saying '…빈 칸, 씨앗이 없어', yet a press plants ('씨앗을 심었어'). This also happens on the base, so it is not a regression, but G1 does not fully close it.
problems.evidence: Both trees: out/st-base.log and out/st-fixed.log, step g1busy. A starts a real walk with APP.importEvents and its plot buttons are visible ([true,true,true], busyA true). After B's claim, la1 is still three times '씨앗이 없어', and pressing btn-plot1 gives toast '씨앗을 심었어' and garden [null,0,null].
problems.suggested_fix: In takeRemote's busy branch, call plotLabels() before `return true`. It reads S only and draws nothing in the scene. Add an X check: start a walk with importEvents, have the second tab claim the weekly gift, and read tab A's labels.

problems.title: Two of E1's three conditions have no failing check
problems.where: js/app.js:4320 (userState: `typeof u.garden[gi].color === 'string' && u.garden[gi].color`); tools/smoke.js step 8b covers only an entry with no colour field
problems.what: Two mutants pass X 43/0. Mutant e1empty drops the non-empty test, so colour '' is kept. Mutant e1type drops the string test, so colour 7 is kept. Without them, a colour '' entry shows as '꽃, 거두기' and is harvested into dyes[''] with the toast '염료 1개를 얻었어', which is the junk key E1 was meant to stop. My base probe shows exactly this.
problems.evidence: runs/mut-e1empty-1.log and runs/mut-e1type-1.log: 43 passed, 0 failed each. Base probe out/st-base.log step e: harvesting the colour '' entry gives dyes {"":1} and the toast '염료 1개를 얻었어'. On the fixed tree (out/st-fixed.log), the same entry shows '빈 칸, 씨앗 심기' and dyes stay {}.
problems.suggested_fix: In the step 8b damaged save, add an entry with color '' and an entry with color 7 among the first three. Expect both to show as '빈 칸', and dyes to have no '' or '7' key after pressing them.

G1: the single call in renderBagChip covers the minute tick and day gift, the tab becoming visible, the weekly claim, another tab's write when not on a walk, import and reset. Checked in code and by the real-timer probe.

P1: the null return applies only when a plot's button is hidden. spotInfo hides a button only when less than 8 px of the plot shows, so taps on visible plots are unchanged (820 regression points identical to the base). When every plot button is hidden, the branch is skipped as before.

P2: the root cause matches the fix agent's account. The closing tab's save reaches the importing tab after the import, with a lower lastSeen. The import itself returned true with the toast '기록을 불러왔어'.

E2: grey #787279 is distinct from all six dye colours (fix agent's OKLab check, plus my look at the day crop next to a blue flower). It is visible at night. The sheet is fine at 320 px in the pixel and plain fonts, light and dark, with no horizontal overflow (scrollWidth equals the viewport width).
Hard lines: no new player-facing text. No requests under audio/ or foley/ and no page errors in any probe.
The new X checks are deterministic: 5 of 5 passes, and step 11 lands on the identical state each run.
